fullPassage:
Hello, listeners. Did you know there are times at night when a massive migration happens right over your heads? The scale of migration involving billions of birds traveling up to thousands of kilometers leaves you in awe. On today's Jo's Tea Time, we invite naturalist and author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge. He's spent decades studying migratory birds, writing about them, and engaging in conservation efforts. Welcome to the show, Mr. Weidensaul.
Thanks for having me, Jo.
Your new book says every spring and fall, hundreds of millions to billions of migratory birds pass over our roofs, but we seem to have no idea that it's happening. Why is that?
Well, most birds migrate after dark, including almost all of the birds that are normally active during the day. That's why it's hard for us to realize the migration is happening. They migrate at night because the night sky is cooler, and the air calmer. Besides, there are fewer predators at night. If you could strip away the night sky and make everything visible, this migration would probably be the largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet.
Among those global travelers in your book, I found the bar-tailed godwits to be particularly impressive.
Sure. Some of them can even make a 10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days.
How do they travel such a long distance over a nearly featureless ocean?
To find their routes, the bar-tailed godwits probably rely on the sun and stars among other things. Some experts believe that they may be able to sense the earth's magnetic field lines, too. You may also wonder how, if ever, they sleep while flying over a vast ocean. It turns out that migratory birds use an approach called "half-brain sleep." This is how it works. Only the left half of the brain sleeps for a couple of seconds, then only the right half for the next couple of seconds, and then this process repeats over and over again. Isn't it amazing? Actually, some sea mammals like dolphins can do that, too, because they have to keep breathing consciously.
That's a neat trick. Who wouldn't like to have such an ability?
Birds in migratory condition can do things that they can't do at other times of the year. Another neat trick you might envy is that they can gain a tremendous amount of muscle tissue without exercise. For example, before some bar-tailed godwits leave Alaska in September and make a 10,000 km flight across the Pacific, they undergo a process of binge feeding. They just eat and eat until they double their weight. By the time they take off, their heart and flight muscles may have increased by 50%. After they have eaten as much as they possibly can and can't put any more weight on, their digestive organs shrink dramatically because these won't be put to use during the non-stop flight to New Zealand.
Then what happens after they arrive there?
They regrow their digestive organs and spend the summer feeding again, and they undergo the same journey back to Alaska. They do this again and again for 25 to 30 years, flying up to 30,000 km every year. By the time bar-tailed godwits die, they have flown close to twice the distance from Earth to the moon.
That's truly impressive. By the way, I hear you've visited Korea several times before. Why do you come here so often?
As a bird watcher and conservationist, I find the Yellow Sea mudflats between Korea and China very special. They are some of the largest tidal mudflats on the earth and provide a critical stopover point for the countless migratory birds on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. While these enormous stretches of tidal mud look featureless to the human eye, they have plenty of marine life forms.
So the mudflats are drawing all kinds of birds in from as far away as New Zealand, Australia, and Asia?
Yes. Many of these birds fly several thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea. Here, they have to double their weight in less than two weeks and make another flight of several thousand kilometers up north. That's why the Yellow Sea is so critically important. It's one of the few places in the world where migratory birds can get the resources they need on their difficult journey.
Oh, I had no idea that the Yellow Sea has such importance. What do you think we can do to preserve this precious gathering place for migratory birds?
Well, you can start by raising awareness of its importance among people around you. Or, if you want to be more actively involved, you can participate in cleaning up beaches or monitoring wildlife habitats. On a bigger scale, because migratory birds travel through many countries, international cooperation is a must for their protection. Actually, I'm working with an international organization consisting of the countries along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. As a result of our international collaboration, we managed to successfully bring back the endangered black-faced spoonbills.
Fascinating! Mr. Weidensaul, today you let us see migratory birds and the Yellow Sea in a whole new way. Thank you!

✅ ① ①

❌ ④ ④

questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ counting → countless: 셀 수 없이 많은 철새를 수식하는 형용사가 필요. counting(세고 있는)은 의미상 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① flying: 분사구문 (부대상황, 정확). ② have flown: by the time + 현재형 → 현재완료 (정확). ③ counting → countless: 'countless migratory birds'가 원문. counting(능동: 세는)이 아니라 countless(셀 수 없는). ④ plenty: plenty of + 명사 (정확).
det.tip: countless = 셀 수 없이 많은 (형용사). counting = 세고 있는 (현재분사). 의미 차이에 주의! by the time + 현재 → 현재완료.

questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ endangering → endangered: 검은머리저어새가 '위험에 처한(endangered)' 상태이므로 과거분사 필요. endangering은 '위험에 빠뜨리는'이라는 능동 의미.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① involved: be involved = 참여하다 (수동/형용사적, 정확). ② consisting: organization consisting of ~ = ~로 구성된 (자동사이므로 능동 분사, 정확). ③ endangering → endangered: spoonbills가 '위험에 빠뜨리는' 것이 아니라 '위험에 처한' 것. 과거분사 필요. ④ let: let + O + V원형 (사역동사, 정확).
det.tip: endangered(위험에 처한, 과거분사) vs endangering(위험에 빠뜨리는, 현재분사). 감정/상태 분사 구별 핵심!

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② halve → double: 먹고 또 먹어서 체중이 두 배(double)가 된다. halve(반으로 줄이다)는 반대 의미.
det.analysis:
✅ ② halve → double: 'eat and eat until they double their weight'가 원문. 폭식으로 체중 두 배. halve(반감)는 반대.
❌ ① tremendous(엄청난): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ increased(증가한): 원문 그대로 50% 증가
❌ ④ shrink(줄어든다): 원문 그대로 소화 기관 축소
det.tip: double(두 배로 하다) ↔ halve(반으로 줄이다). 폭식(binge feeding) → 체중 증가(double) 맥락.

questions.passage: Oh, I had no idea that the Yellow Sea has such importance. What do you think we can do to preserve this precious gathering place for migratory birds? questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ isolation → cooperation: 국제적 협력(cooperation)이 보호를 위해 필수이다. isolation(고립)은 cooperation(협력)의 반대.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ isolation → cooperation: 여러 나라를 통과하므로 '협력'이 필요. '고립'은 보호 맥락과 모순.
❌ ① awareness(인식): 원문 그대로. 인식 제고
❌ ② monitoring(모니터링): 원문 그대로. 서식지 모니터링
❌ ④ endangered(멸종 위기의): 원문 그대로
det.tip: cooperation(협력) ↔ isolation(고립/격리). international cooperation = 국제 협력. 철새가 여러 나라를 통과하므로 국제적 협력이 핵심.

det.korean: 이 이동은 아마도 지구상 가장 크고 위대한 자연 장관(spectacle)일 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ spectacle(장관): 'the largest, greatest'와 어울리는 긍정적 표현. 눈에 보이게 만들면 대단한 볼거리
❌ ① disaster(재난): 새의 이동을 재난이라 하는 것은 부적절
❌ ② obstacle(장애물): 이동 자체가 장애물이라는 것은 비논리적
❌ ③ mystery(신비): 보이게 만들면 '장관'이지 '신비'가 아님
det.tip: spectacle = 장관, 볼거리. 'the largest, greatest natural spectacle' = 가장 크고 위대한 자연의 장관. strip away = 벗기다.

questions.passage: As a bird watcher and conservationist, I find the Yellow Sea mudflats between Korea and China very special. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 인간의 눈에는 특징 없어(featureless) 보이지만 풍부한 해양 생물이 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② featureless(특징 없는): While(~에도 불구하고) + look featureless + they have plenty of → 역접. 특징 없어 보이지만 실제로 풍부
❌ ① spectacular(장관인): '하지만 풍부하다'와 역접이 성립하지 않음
❌ ③ colorful(화려한): 역접 구조상 부정적 외관이 와야 함
❌ ④ threatening(위협적인): 갯벌이 위협적이라는 것은 맥락에 맞지 않음
det.tip: While A, B = A이지만 B. 역접 구조에서 A(부정적 외관) ↔ B(긍정적 실제). featureless(특징 없어 보이는) ↔ plenty of marine life(풍부한 해양 생물).

ch: 큰뒷부리도요는 태양과 별에 의존하여 경로를 찾는다.

det.korean: ③ 태양과 별에 의존: the bar-tailed godwits probably rely on the sun and stars.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 일치: 'rely on the sun and stars among other things' — 태양과 별에 의존.
❌ ① 대서양: 원문은 Pacific Ocean(태평양).
❌ ② 동부 알래스카: 원문은 western Alaska(서부 알래스카).
❌ ④ 중력: 원문은 magnetic field(자기장). gravity(중력)가 아님.
det.tip: Pacific Ocean(태평양) ≠ Atlantic Ocean(대서양). western(서부) ≠ eastern(동부). magnetic field(자기장) ≠ gravity(중력).

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ① 돌고래도 반뇌수면 가능: some sea mammals like dolphins can do that, too.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 일치: dolphins can do that, too — 돌고래도 반뇌수면 가능.
❌ ② 동시: only the left → then only the right. 교대로 잠든다.
❌ ③ 1분 단위: a couple of seconds(몇 초). 1분이 아님.

det.tip: a couple of seconds = 몇 초. consciously(의식적으로) ↔ unconsciously(무의식적으로). 돌고래가 반뇌수면을 하는 이유 = 의식적 호흡 유지.

det.korean: 함축: 일생에 걸친 비행 거리가 상상을 초월할 만큼 엄청나다. 지구~달 거리의 두 배라는 비유적 표현.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 엄청난 비행 거리: 지구~달 거리의 약 두 배(약 770,000km)를 비행한다는 것은 비행 거리의 경이로움을 강조
❌ ① 우주 여행: 비유적 표현이지 실제 우주 여행이 아님
❌ ② 달까지 거리가 가깝다: 거리의 두 배를 비행한다는 것은 '멀다'는 강조
❌ ③ 측정 불가능: 실제로 30,000km × 25~30년으로 계산 가능
det.tip: 함축의미 추론: 비유적 표현의 의도를 파악. '지구~달 거리의 두 배'는 실제 우주 여행이 아니라 비행 거리의 경이로움을 강조하는 수사적 표현.

questions.passage: After they have eaten as much as they possibly can, their digestive organs shrink dramatically. They regrow their digestive organs and spend the summer feeding again, and they undergo the same journey back to Alaska. They do this again and again for 25 to 30 years, flying up to 30,000 km every year. By the time bar-tailed godwits die, <u>they</u> have flown close to twice the distance from Earth to the moon. That's truly impressive.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 'they'가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: they = 큰뒷부리도요(bar-tailed godwits). 앞 문장들의 주어가 계속 큰뒷부리도요.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ bar-tailed godwits: 문맥상 'By the time bar-tailed godwits die, they have flown ~'에서 they = bar-tailed godwits.
❌ ① 인터뷰어와 게스트: 비행하지 않음.
❌ ② 돌고래: 비행하지 않음.
❌ ④ 해양 생물: 비행하지 않음.
det.tip: 대명사 they의 선행사를 찾을 때: 가장 가까운 복수명사 + 문맥상 의미가 통하는 것을 선택. have flown(비행한)과 연결되는 주어.

questions.passage: While these enormous stretches of tidal mud look featureless to the human eye, they have plenty of marine life forms. So the mudflats are drawing all kinds of birds in from as far away as New Zealand, Australia, and Asia? Yes. Many of <u>these birds</u> fly several thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea. Here, they have to double their weight in less than two weeks.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 'these birds'가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 인간의 눈에 보이지 않는 해양 생물들

det.korean: these birds = 황해 갯벌로 날아오는 철새들. 뉴질랜드, 호주, 아시아 등에서 날아오는 새들.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 황해 갯벌로 날아오는 철새들: 'drawing all kinds of birds in from as far away as New Zealand, Australia, and Asia'에서 이 새들을 가리킴.
❌ ② 큰뒷부리도요만: 다양한 종류의 새(all kinds of birds)를 포함.
❌ ③ 해양 생물: 새가 아님.
❌ ④ 텃새: migratory birds(철새)이지 텃새가 아님.
det.tip: these birds는 앞 문장 'all kinds of birds in from as far away as New Zealand, Australia, and Asia'를 받는다. 특정 종이 아닌 다양한 철새.

questions.passage: They are some of the largest tidal mudflats on the earth and provide a critical stopover point for the countless migratory birds on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. While these enormous stretches of tidal mud look featureless to the human eye, they have plenty of marine life forms. So the mudflats are drawing all kinds of birds in from as far away as New Zealand, Australia, and Asia? Yes. Many of these birds fly several thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea. Here, they have to double their weight in less than two weeks and make another flight of several thousand kilometers up north. That's why the Yellow Sea is so critically important. It's one of the few places in the world where migratory birds can get the resources they need on their difficult journey.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 뜻에 해당하는 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"a large, flat area of mud that is uncovered when the tide goes out"

det.korean: mudflats = 갯벌, 간석지. 조수가 빠지면 드러나는 넓고 평평한 진흙 지대.
det.analysis: mudflats = 갯벌. 영영 풀이: 조수가 빠지면 드러나는 넓고 평평한 진흙 지대. tidal mudflats = 조간대 갯벌.
det.tip: mudflat(갯벌) = mud(진흙) + flat(평평한 곳). tidal(조수의) + mudflat = 조간대 갯벌.

questions.passage: As a result of our international collaboration, we managed to successfully bring back the [endanger] black-faced spoonbills. Fascinating! Mr. Weidensaul, today you let us see migratory birds and the Yellow Sea in a whole new way.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형을 변환하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: 멸종 위기의(endangered) 검은머리저어새를 복원했다. endanger(동사) → endangered(과거분사/형용사).
det.analysis: the [형용사] black-faced spoonbills 구조. 명사를 수식하는 형용사 자리. endanger(위험에 빠뜨리다) → endangered(위험에 처한/멸종 위기의). 과거분사가 형용사로 쓰임.
det.tip: endanger(동사: 위험에 빠뜨리다) → endangered(형용사: 멸종 위기의). endangered species = 멸종 위기 종. 감정/상태의 과거분사 형용사.

questions.passage: Well, most birds migrate after dark, including almost all of the birds that are normally active during the day. That's why it's hard for us to realize the migration is happening. They migrate at night because the night sky is cooler, and the air calmer. Besides, there are fewer predators at night. If you could strip away the night sky and make everything visible, this migration would probably be the largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet.
questions.stem: 새들이 밤에 이동하는 이유로 언급되지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 별빛이 경로를 밝혀줌 — 본문에 언급되지 않은 이유. 이동 이유는 ①시원함 ②잔잔함 ③적은 포식자.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 별빛이 경로를 밝혀줌: 본문에서 별은 경로 탐색(rely on the sun and stars)에서 언급되지만, 밤에 이동하는 '이유'로는 언급되지 않음.
❌ ① cooler: 밤하늘이 더 시원 — 이유로 언급됨.
❌ ② calmer: 공기가 더 잔잔 — 이유로 언급됨.
❌ ③ fewer predators: 포식자가 적음 — 이유로 언급됨.
det.tip: NOT 문제: '언급되지 않은 것'을 찾아야 함. 별에 의존하는 것은 경로 찾기(navigation)이지 밤 이동의 이유가 아님.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 본문의 표현을 활용하여 영작하시오.

"그 과정이 계속해서 반복된다."

→ This process __________ over and over again.

det.korean: 이 과정이 계속해서 반복된다(repeats).
det.analysis: 원문: 'this process repeats over and over again'. this process(3인칭 단수) + repeats(3인칭 단수 동사). over and over again = 계속해서.
det.tip: repeat = 반복하다. this process(단수 주어) → repeats(3인칭 단수 -s). over and over again = 반복적으로.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 본문의 표현을 활용하여 영작하시오.

"인식을 높이는 것부터 시작할 수 있다."

→ You can start by __________ awareness.

det.korean: 인식을 높이는(raising awareness) 것부터 시작할 수 있다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'you can start by raising awareness of its importance'. start by + V-ing = ~하는 것부터 시작하다. raise awareness = 인식을 높이다.
det.tip: start by + V-ing = ~하는 것부터 시작하다. raise awareness = 인식을 제고하다. by(전치사) 뒤에 동명사(-ing)가 옴.
